//: TLM INIT DOC — the pre-filled answer sheet for a project's FIRST /tlm-project-setup.
WHO FILLS THIS IN: whoever already set the project up (the lead). Everything here is a
decision that was made once and must be the SAME for everyone — the tracker, the status
vocabulary, the base branch, the release channel, the sibling repos. A teammate who answers
those questions again is a teammate who answers one of them differently.
HOW IT IS USED: send this file with the init command. The teammate saves it into the project
as .claude/tlm-init.json and runs  /tlm-project-setup init  — every value below is applied
WITHOUT a question, and they are asked only for what a file cannot carry: their own Figma
token, and clicking Connect on the OAuth connectors.
GENERATING IT INSTEAD OF TYPING IT (recommended): in a project that is already configured,
node <rulesRoot>/skills/tlm-project-setup/init.mjs template --from-current --out ~/tlm-init.json
That reads .claude/settings.local.json, strips secrets and per-machine paths, and prints the
handover message to paste alongside the file.
RULES FOR EDITING THIS FILE
1. Leave a <<FILL: …>> marker anywhere you do not have the value. A marker is treated as
UNANSWERED — it is never imported, and /tlm-project-setup asks for it as usual. That is the
safe state; a placeholder imported as if it were real looks configured and fails later.
2. Delete nothing. An `enabled: false` is an ANSWERED no and is never re-asked; a deleted
block is an unasked question and comes back.
3. Do NOT add `permissions`, `hooks` or `enabledPlugins` here. They are refused on import —
a file that arrives over chat is not how a teammate grants tool access.
4. Secrets are per-user by default (see $tlmInit.secrets). Sharing one Figma token makes
every read look like yours and breaks the whole team the day it is rotated.
5. This file is NOT committed. /tlm-project-setup gitignores it, and `init.mjs consume` deletes
it once applied. It goes stale the moment the config changes — reissue, don't archive.
Every key below is documented in ./tlm-config.reference.json. This doc's shape IS a
settings.local.json (`env` + `tlm`) plus the $tlmInit block, so there is no second schema.

$tlmInit.createdBy: <<FILL: your name — shown to the teammate so they know the file is yours>>
$tlmInit.createdFor: <<FILL: which project / team this is for>>
$tlmInit.//secrets: per-user = each teammate supplies their own token (the env values below stay markers). included = you deliberately put real tokens in this file; then treat it as a credential and send it the way you would send a password.
$tlmInit.notes: <<FILL: anything they should know — e.g. 'connect ClickUp first, the rest is done'>>
howToUse: Save this file into the project as .claude/tlm-init.json
Everything in it is applied without asking; you are asked only for what it cannot carry.

//env: SECRETS. Kept as markers under secrets:'per-user' — the teammate generates their own and
/tlm-project-setup writes it to their gitignored settings.local.json.
A value already present on the teammate's machine ALWAYS wins over one in this file.

env.FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN: <<FILL: per-user — Figma → avatar → Settings → Security → Personal access tokens → Generate, scope 'File content'; starts with figd_>>
env.//CONTEXT7_API_KEY: OPTIONAL and per-user — context7 works without it; a key only raises rate limits. Leave the marker (it is dropped on import) unless a teammate wants to add their own from https://context7.com/dashboard.
env.CONTEXT7_API_KEY: <<FILL: optional per-user context7 key (ctx7sk-…) — leave as-is to skip>>

tlm.//project: name/type/baseBranch. type is PHASE 1 question 1 — filling it here skips that question.

project.name: <<FILL: human-readable project name, e.g. Telemax Installer>>
project.type: <<FILL: nextjs-page-router | nextjs-app-router | react-native-expo | react-native-cli | flutter | other>>
project.//apps: MONOREPO ONLY — one entry per app so release notes can tell which app a commit range belongs to. Leave the markers in place for a single-app repo and they are dropped.

tlm.//design: PHASE 1 question 3a. enabled:false is an answered no — tlm-figma-to-code then never asks for a token.
//tickets: PHASE 1 question 2 plus everything the tracker needs. The statuses are the values worth
carrying most: they are the team's real vocabulary, they differ per workspace, and a
teammate guessing them moves tickets into a status your board does not have.
workspaceId + urlTemplate both come out of ANY ticket URL: https://app.clickup.com/t/<workspaceId>/TLM-1234

tickets.idPattern: <<FILL: regex for ticket ids in commits, e.g. TLM-\d+>>

statuses.inProgress: <<FILL: the exact status name work-started uses>>
statuses.inReview: <<FILL: the exact status name submitted-for-review uses>>
ready: <<FILL: the statuses that mean safe to ship>>

tickets.defaultListId: <<FILL: ClickUp list id where tlm-ba-ticket creates new tickets — optional, asked on first run if absent>>

tlm.//chat: PHASE 1 question 3b. sendMode stays 'draft' — a human reviews before anything reaches a shared channel. One channel entry per app; `app` matches a project.apps[].name.

channels.app: <<FILL: app name, or drop this field for a single-app repo>>
channels.id: <<FILL: Slack → open channel → View channel details → id at the bottom (C…)>>
channels.name: <<FILL: #channel-name>>

//specDriven: Left out on purpose. It is DETECTED from an openspec/ directory in the repo being set up —
carrying it here would claim tlm-spec-driven for a project that has no openspec/. Add the block
only if you know the target repo is already on OpenSpec.
//ecosystem: PHASE 1 question 4 — the other repos of this system Claude may READ while working here.
This is the highest-value part of the handover: a guessed endpoint shape or shared type
passes review and breaks at runtime, and only the lead knows which repos matter.
Give a gitUrl (it is cloned shallow into workspaceRoot on the teammate's machine) — NOT a
path, which is where the repo happens to live on YOUR machine. workspaceRoot is per-machine
and deliberately absent so each machine keeps its own default (~/tlm-ecosystem).
Standalone project? Set enabled:false and delete nothing else.

repos.name: <<FILL: short repo name, also the clone directory>>
repos.role: <<FILL: backend | web | mobile | shared-lib | design-system | infra | docs>>
repos.gitUrl: <<FILL: clone URL the teammate can actually reach>>
repos.notes: <<FILL: what THIS project uses from it — 'owns the endpoint DTOs in src/modules/**/dto'>>

//pluginRepo: The project's live rules copy (.claude/tlm-plugin/) and the contribute-back PR target.
enabled:true is the default and /tlm-project-setup installs the copy itself.
upstreamRemote MUST be a URL that resolves on the TEAMMATE's machine. The plugin default is
an SSH host alias (git@github.com-hbl:…) that only exists in the ~/.ssh/config of whoever
set it up — if your team does not share that alias, put the https:// or plain git@ URL here.
A value the teammate already has is never overwritten by this file.

pluginRepo.upstreamRemote: <<FILL: git URL of the plugin upstream that works on their machine>>
